## A refused API key asks for a new one

When the API refuses your key - a Private Pro subscription ended, a key was
revoked or mistyped - the integration used to report a failed update and leave
every entity unavailable. Home Assistant now shows it as needing
re-authentication instead. Enter a new key there, or leave the field empty to
carry on with public access and its 48-hour horizon. A network problem is not
mistaken for a bad key: that still simply retries.

## Old data says that it is old

When a request fails, the integration keeps the last good data - an hour-old
forecast is still a forecast. It just never said so. The **price series**
sensor and the **current retail price** sensor now carry two attributes:
`data_status` is `fresh` when the last request for that series succeeded and
`stale` when the data is from an earlier one, and `data_updated` is when it
last arrived. A card or an automation can check for `stale` before trusting
the series.

## Diagnostics that answer the first questions

The diagnostics file now lists, per data source, when it last succeeded, how
old its data is and what last went wrong. It also checks every series for
gaps and overlaps and names the times involved - which is exactly what a
missing hour around a change of daylight-saving time looks like (see issue
#6). Your API key and postal code are removed from it, including from error
messages. Tests now cover both changes of time, the 25-hour and the 23-hour
day.

## Planning five days ahead, explained

The README now says up front what the forecast reaches - 48 hours free, up to
120 hours with Private Pro - who gains from the extra days, and what they were
worth, measured: in Germany, choosing the charging day among four days instead
of two was cheaper on 12 of 29 autumn evenings and dearer on 2, 2.43 ct/kWh
less on average. A copyable prompt lets an AI assistant work out whether that
is worth it for your own devices. The ready-made dashboard card ends with a
one-line pointer to the longer horizon, shown only while yours is below 120
hours.

## A shorter README

The README keeps installation, the entities, the horizon, which plan to use
and support. Tariffs, forecast quality, entity details and the dashboard
chapter with its cards moved to `docs/`, each linked from where it used to
be. Bug reports now open with a short form asking for the version, market and
time zone, and take the diagnostics file.

## Tested against old and new Home Assistant

Every change is now tested against Home Assistant 2025.6 - the oldest this
integration supports - and the current release.

## Updating from 1.16.x

Nothing to do. The two new attributes appear on their own. Existing dashboard
cards keep working; to get the new footer line, paste the card again from
`examples/price-card.yaml`.
